original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Independently recompute the merged forward/backward cone cut from the pinned witness and certificate with a separately written checker: 2,309 edges, marker counts 25/52/365/1725, forward cone 1,725, backward seeds 12, growth 12/22/37, empty intersection, 37-edge digest; then compare the one-step result with fixed-point closures of the same relations. No construction, no complete bill, no kappa.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags can be realized by a chronological correction program. That program is not attempted. The work here is a bounded independent recomputation of one merged finite receipt inside the same fixed-cover route (`research/p104-cone-cut`), chosen because the receipt is new, carries the missing-pair finding for the 4,992 required pairs, and had no independent check. The connection is stated in README: same frozen witness, certificate and relation; no construction, restoration or bill is supplied.
bottleneck_link: The fixed-cover route is still the live P104 obligation (the family record asks for review of the submitted support cut before the contract is treated as closed). The merged cone-cut receipt is one of the finite inputs to that decision: it records that the missing pair target 71 from source 102 is not reached by either cone. An independent recomputation raises or lowers confidence in that input; the saturation comparison records exactly how far the emptiness may be strengthened. This is verification-side evidence, not a mechanism improvement.
stop_rule: Stop at the published receipt values: reproduce all eight merged fields, the two inherited counts, and the closure comparison. Do not attempt the chronological program, the physical bill, the 4,992-pair accumulation or a new search. If any value disagreed, report the disagreement and stop.
evidence: verify.py reproduces every published merged value and both inherited counts, and the fixed-point closures of the same relations meet the one-step forward cone (26 edges) and contain its 37 backward edges (README table and RESULT.json). test_verify.py holds four controls that reject a weakened relation and changed source/target labels. Local runs: verify about 20 s, controls about 35 s under CPython 3.12.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the one-step emptiness survive a scheduled variant that applies two expansion steps at one dimension and none at another?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The saturation comparison shows an unbounded same-dimension closure does not preserve the emptiness; the intermediate schedules decide whether the cut can be strengthened at all.
open_questions.first_step: Add a step-count parameter per dimension to the transfer and scan the small schedules at dimensions 8, 7 and 6.
open_questions.blocked_by: None locally; the merged receipt does not commit to any schedule beyond one step per dimension.

open_questions.question: Do the 26 meeting edges carry any of the 4,992 required pairs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If a closure-reachable edge carries a required pair, the schedule sensitivity has content for the missing-pair question; if not, it is a structural remark only.
open_questions.first_step: Overlay the accumulated required-pair list on the 26 meeting edges (the accumulation itself lives in the missing-pair lineage and is not re-derived here).
open_questions.blocked_by: The required-pair accumulation is not part of this package.

open_questions.question: Do the literal and interval recurrences both reach the same 4,991 of 4,992 required pairs under this independent code path?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two merged readings are the same adjacency claim executed twice; an independent third implementation of the accumulation would close the loop.
open_questions.first_step: Implement the required-pair accumulation directly from the certificate masks and compare counts.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of scope here; needs the union-support accumulation contract.
